4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

A.  NO RIGHT-TURN ON RED AT THE NORTHWEST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AND PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

Lynn Yen, a resident of Rolling Hills Estates, stated that she would like the Traffic and Safety
Committee to consider a “No Right Turn on Red” from Palos Verdes Drive East southbound,
turning westbound onto Palos Verdes Drive North. She stated that she has continued to observe
that when children are crossing from Dapplegray Park (northwest corner) to Founder’s Park
(northeast corner), a driver’s visibility is difficult for the pedestrians who are crossing the street,
since their focus is on the traffic. She added that if a “No Right Turn on Red” were installed, drivers
would be forced to stop instead of inching up into the intersection.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, September 17, 2025
 CHAIR PAM BROWN SCHACHTER asked if Ms. Yen has a recommendation for a time frame for
the “No Right Turn on Red”. Ms. Yen suggested this condition for the period both before and after
school, and possibly some hours on the weekends, for people crossing to the parks and the future
Nature Center. CHAIR PAM BROWN SCHACHTER stated that this item will be placed on a future
Traffic and Safety meeting agenda.

Amy Dempster Fitzpatrick, a resident of Rolling Hills Estates, stated that she lives on the south
side of Palos Verdes Drive North on Rolling Meadows Road. She stated that she recently moved
back to the area and walks her three children to Rancho Vista School each morning. She noted
that on the south side of Palos Verdes Drive North at Rolling Meadows Road there is no path or
walkway from Rolling Meadows Road to get to the crosswalks that are to the east and west of
Rolling Meadows Road. She stated that the only option is to walk uphill for half a mile to the top
of Rolling Meadows Road and walk down to the crosswalk at Silver Spur Road and across Palos
Verdes Drive North. Ms. Fitzpatrick requested that the City conduct a traffic survey and feasibility
of a crosswalk, with flashing safety lights across Palos Verdes Drive North to improve visibility.

Rory and CeCe Fitzpatrick, children of Ms. Fitzpatrick, expressed that it is difficult to cross the
street because the cars are going fast and they must wait for a gap in traffic in order to cross.

In response to a question from CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Ms. Fitzpatrick stated that there
are children from other schools who share the same concerns.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that staff would need to research if this is feasible and this
will be added to a future Traffic and Safety Committee meeting agenda.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  SPEED LIMIT DISCUSSION ON PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH

Director Naughton stated that at its May 19, 2025 meeting the Traffic and Safety Committee
considered reducing the speed limit on Palos Verdes Drive North from the eastern City boundary
to Hawthorne Blvd. to and at that time staff recommended that an inventory be conducted of the
number of signs that would require replacement, with estimated replacement cost, which is
outlined in the staff report. She stated that Willdan provided an amendment to their 2021 survey
report, which is the required justification that needs to be included along with the recommendation
to the City Council.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene provided a presentation summarizing the staff report including
an overview of Assembly Bill 43 (AB 43). He stated that AB 43 provides cities with more flexibility
in setting local speed limits. Agencies are now allowed to lower speed limits by up to 5 miles per
hour under certain conditions. To qualify for these reductions, the roadway must be designated
as a safety corridor or as an area with a high concentration of bicyclists or pedestrians. He stated
that speed limits must still be based on the 85th percentile speed, which is determined through
traffic surveys. The maximum allowable reduction from the 85th percentile speed is 12.4 miles
per hour. Willdan went through the process for setting and revising speed limits as outlined in the
guidelines established in the California Vehicle Code and the California Manual on Uniform Traffic
Control Devices (MUTCD) and determined the latest revisions.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, September 17, 2025
 In response to a question from Will Nicklas, Planning Commissioner, Traffic Engineering Deputy
Greene explained how the 85th percentile is calculated, which is the speed that 85% of the
vehicles are travelling.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that staff reviewed the speed survey data and made
recommendations for adjustments. It was noted that the east segment of the drive cannot be
lowered further and will remain at 40 mph, while the remaining segments from Palos Verdes Drive
East to Hawthorne Boulevard are recommended to be reduced to 35 mph.

Director Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Traffic and Safety Committee confirm
the recommendation to the City Council and that it approves the reduction of the speed limit on
Palos Verdes Drive North as follows:

  •  The segment commencing at the eastern boundary of the city to the intersection of Palos
  Verdes Drive East and Palos Verdes Drive North would go from 45 mph to 40 mph.
  •  The segment commencing at that intersection to the intersection of Hawthorne Blvd. and
  Palos Verdes Drive North would go from 40 mph to 35 mph.
  •  To receive and file the speed sign survey and survey data from the 2021 Engineering
  and Traffic Survey and the 2025 amendment report.
In response to a suggestion from CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that
staff will take a look at the condition of the existing signs to determine if they could be reused.
COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE asked for clarification on the speed limit on Palos Verdes Drive
North from the east City limit to Palos Verdes Drive East going from 45 mph to 40 mph as opposed
to lowering it to 35 mph and asked if this could be reconsidered. Traffic Engineering Deputy
Greene stated that this was the request and there are no issues making a 10-mph change.
Commissioner Nicklas added that there are issues with the speed of vehicles when getting out
from Montecillo onto Palos Verdes Drive North.

A brief discussion ensued on several issues with the speed on Palos Verdes Drive North.

COMMITTEE MEMBER PERSICHINA asked about the number of speeding tickets issued on
Palos Verdes Drive North. Deputy Gamboa stated that he does not have the information on- hand,
however, he and other deputies issue several tickets per day/week.

In response to a question from CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Deputy Gamboa stated that when
school is in session, their department receives requests for increased patrol in the area.

In response to a question from Commissioner Nicklas, CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that
electronic speed signs have been discussed.

A brief discussion ensued on the speed limit signs.

In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER TERTZAKIAN, Director Naughton stated
that the change to speed limits will be widely published through public notices including a
comment period, city website, social media, and newsletters. COMMITTEE MEMBER HALL
suggested having the mobile electronic sign with the new speed limit.

COMMITTEE MEMBER ROWE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS
to,

   ADD ILLUMINATED FRAME SPEED LIMIT SIGNS ON WESTBOUND PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AT THE LOCATIONS WHERE THE SPEED LIMIT CHANGES TO 40
  MPH, AND WHERE THE SPEED LIMIT CHANGES TO 35 MPH, AND A THIRD SIGN AT
  THE RANCHVIEW ROAD INTERSECTION.

AYES:  Brown Schachter, Combs, Hall, Martin, Munday, Nash, Olson, Persichina, Rowe,
  Tertzakian
NOES:
ABSENT:  Halvorsen
ABSTAIN:

B.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH AND SILVER SADDLE LANE PEDESTRIAN
  CROSSING (VERBAL REPORT)

Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene stated that at the last meeting there was a request from a
resident to install a HAWK (high-intensity activated crosswalk beacon) at the intersection of Palos
Verdes Drive North and Silver Saddle Lane for pedestrian crossing. At that meeting, the
committee requested that staff pull collision data for this intersection prior to conducting a full
traffic study. Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene requested data from the Los Angeles County
Sheriff’s Department. The data collected was from January 2017 through August 2025, and there
were five reported collisions and of those collisions, one had a recorded injury; no collisions
involved pedestrians. According to the data, there is no compelling data to make a change at this
intersection.

In response to a request from CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER, Traffic Engineering Deputy Greene
explained how the HAWK beacon works.

A brief discussion ensued on this item. No further action was taken.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER noted that since Chadwick School now has parents park at the
South Coast Botanic Gardens and children are bused to school, the traffic has improved
considerably.

CHAIR BROWN SCHACHTER stated that the City of Rancho Palos Verdes was considering
speed enforcement cameras but have since dropped it. There was no interest from the committee
in considering this in the City.

Deputy Gamboa stated that earlier in the week he was parked in front of Rolling Hills Covenant
Church on Palos Verdes Drive North and pursued two vehicles racing at speeds of approximately
95 mph. Upon catching up to the vehicles, he received calls about two collisions that he had to
respond to. Deputy Gamboa wrote a report on the speeding vehicles, and a judge signed a

 warrant to seize the vehicles for 30 days, which will also result in a $2,000 impound fee. In this
instance there were no citations, however two vehicles will be seized as an alternative, which can
be more effective in deterring speeding in the area.
